premieres.label: North American premiere
premieres.note: REGARD's Grand Prize rides on it

premieres.label: US premiere
premieres.note: Tribeca's award track rides on it

premieres.label: France unscreened
premieres.note: A Clermont screening spends it — closes both Cannes doors

festivals.name: Sundance 2027
festivals.why: No premiere requirement, and the eligibility rule — completed after Dec 31, 2025 — makes a Jan 2026 film the exact intended cohort. AFI theses land here regularly. The single most urgent submission on this board. Submission note: Confirmed: sundance.org submit page explicitly directs applicants to FilmFreeway (filmfreeway.com/Sundance) for the 2027 Festival; no separate proprietary portal used for festival entries.

festivals.name: PAFF 2027
festivals.why: Largest Black film festival in the US; 'films by and/or about people of African descent' is the thesis statement. Deadline ladder could NOT be verified — may close ~Aug 31. Caution: an LA screening here spends the LA premiere that ABFF and HollyShorts require.

festivals.name: Tampere 57th
festivals.why: European big-three shorts festival, qualifying on Grand Prix and Best Fiction, no premiere requirement, nearly free. Early bird Sep 1.

festivals.name: Atlanta FF 51st
festivals.why: Major Southern festival with a deep Black film community; jury award confers Oscar qualification; no premiere requirement. Keep the film out of greater Atlanta until it screens here.

festivals.name: Flickerfest 36th
festivals.why: Qualifying via Best International Short plus a 40-city Australian tour. Requires an Australian premiere (intact) and the film off the open internet.

festivals.name: SXSW 2027
festivals.why: The fight-ring engine and ancestral visions give it a genre hook; premiere status is a preference, not a rule, so it layers cleanly behind Sundance. Submission note: own portal: cart.sxsw.com (SXSW Cart film application system, e.g. cart.sxsw.com/products/filmapp-short). No FilmFreeway page exists for the Austin flagship festival - only spinoff events (SXSW Sydney, SXSW London) use FilmFreeway.

festivals.name: Carthage JCC 37th
festivals.why: Oldest African/Arab festival; Tanit shorts competition historically reserved for African and Arab films. Eligibility of a US-produced film by a Nigerian director needs a one-line email to the festival before entering. Submission note: own portal: inscription.jcc.tn (mirrored at inscription.jcctunisie.org). Confirmed jcc.tn is the current official site (37th edition, Dec 12-19 2026); jcctunisie.org domain had DNS resolution issues at check time.

festivals.name: SBIFF 42nd
festivals.why: Qualifying in all three shorts categories with an awards-season industry crowd; notification Jan 8 lands after Sundance's decision, so it slots into either outcome.

festivals.name: FESPACO 30th
festivals.why: The most prestigious pan-African festival, biennial — miss it and the next door is 2029. Open to diaspora directors; the 2027 theme is cultural self-reclamation. Oscar-qualifying only for documentary shorts, so this is canon prestige, not an Academy path. Submission note: own portal: fespaco.bf itself hosts registration via the national 'Faso Arzeka' platform (ABCA). Registration open Feb 24-Sep 20, 2026 for the Feb-Mar 2027 30th edition.

festivals.name: Clermont-Ferrand 49th
festivals.why: The world's largest shorts stage; no premiere requirement; every submitted film enters the Marché catalogue browsed by 5,000 industry pros. One chess note: a Clermont screening is a French screening — it closes the Cannes doors (see the France lock). Submission note: own/third-party portal: ShortFilmDepot (shortfilmdepot.com) - NOT FilmFreeway. Confirmed via official lecourt-clermont.org submit page; deadline for 49th edition (Jan 29-Feb 6 2027) was Sept 24, 2026.

festivals.name: Aspen Shortsfest 36th
festivals.why: One of the two most prestigious US shorts-only festivals; Best Drama is the exact qualifying lane. Cannot have premiered before Apr 2026 (fine) and must stay off the US internet.

festivals.name: Cleveland CIFF51
festivals.why: Qualifies in all three shorts categories; huge civic audience. Requires only a Cleveland premiere.

festivals.name: Florida FF 36th
festivals.why: Cheapest earlybird on the board ($35) with Grand Jury qualification for majority-US-funded narrative shorts. Florida premiere needed for competition.

festivals.name: College Television Awards 46th
festivals.why: The 46th window should cover work completed Aug 2025–Jul 2026 — a Jan 2026 finish fits — with submissions estimated late Sep–early Oct 2026. Verify at televisionacademy.com now; the window is weeks long. Submission note: own portal: TelevisionAcademy.com/CTA/submit (Television Academy Foundation's own submission system). No FilmFreeway listing found despite specific search.

festivals.name: Joburg FF 9th
festivals.why: Only African and African-diaspora filmmakers may submit — a curated-for-you audience with MultiChoice pan-African reach. The call likely opens within days.

festivals.name: Toronto Black FF
festivals.why: Canada's flagship Black film festival; international diaspora programming. Registration deadline Nov 1 per the festival's own site.

festivals.name: REGARD 31st
festivals.why: Qualifying on both its Grand Prizes, and it explicitly prioritizes premiere-intact films not free online — which this is. The Grand Prize (the Oscar path) is limited to World/North American/Canadian premieres, so submit before spending the NA premiere. Submission note: own portal: form.zonefestival.com (Zone Festival submission system, e.g. form.zonefestival.com/?k=regard_f8ls) - NOT FilmFreeway.

festivals.name: Berlinale Shorts 77th
festivals.why: The most politically engaged A-list shorts competition — a slave-revolt film reclaiming Yoruba faith is squarely its taste, and the Golden Bear qualifies. US-only screenings preserve the international-premiere status it requires, so Sundance-first keeps it alive. The 12-month completion window nominally cuts ~Feb 2026 — enter with the final-deliverables date (see Playbook). Submit blind Nov 4, before Sundance notifies. Submission note: own portal: berlinale.de's own online Film Entry system (My Film Entry account). Confirmed via official Berlinale Shorts regulations page - no FilmFreeway involvement.

festivals.name: Krakow FF 67th
festivals.why: Triple-qualifying (Oscar, EFA, BAFTA). Timing trap: films completed before Oct 31, 2026 must enter by the FIRST phase (~Nov 30, 2026) — the later January deadline is not for this film. Submission note: own portal: krakowfilmfestival.pl 'MyKFF' filmmaker account/login system. No FilmFreeway page exists for the main Krakow Film Festival (distinct from other Krakow-based fests like Mastercard OFF CAMERA or Krakow Mountain Festival, which do use FilmFreeway).

festivals.name: Luxor African FF 16th
festivals.why: Shorts competition restricted to African directors — the Nigerian director qualifies, and diaspora heritage stories are staple programming. Open now, free. Submission note: own portal: Google Form at forms.gle/XHudKudvVQvUuBJe8, linked directly from the official site's Submit Your Film page. No FilmFreeway page found for this festival.

festivals.name: Seattle SIFF 2027
festivals.why: Top-5 US audience festival, qualifying in all three shorts categories. Only a Western Washington premiere required.

festivals.name: Vienna Shorts 2027
festivals.why: Quadruple-qualifying (Oscar, EFA, BAFTA, Austrian FA); Fiction & Documentary competition is a legitimate home. Arthouse taste — a coin-flip fit.

festivals.name: ABFF — HBO Short Film Award
festivals.why: 30th year of the award; five finalists screen for a jury in front of HBO/WBD and streamer scouts; $10,000 grand prize and the winner qualifies for the 100th Academy Awards. Requires LA-premiere status at screening and no US online release before May 23, 2027 — this is the door the LA premiere should be saved for.

festivals.name: Tribeca 2027
festivals.why: Large narrative shorts slate, deep diaspora programming, NYC industry. Catch: award (Oscar) eligibility historically needs a US premiere — a Sundance screening removes the award path, leaving exposure only. Decide after Sundance notifies. Submission note: Confirmed: Tribeca accepts via both its own Extranet portal and FilmFreeway; note the reduced student short-film fee is Extranet-only.

festivals.name: Cannes — La Cinef 2027
festivals.why: Purpose-built door for conservatory thesis films; the 18-month window covers a Jan 2026 lock. Decided: the campaign doesn't wait for it — it enters by Feb 15 only if Sundance and Clermont both pass, since any non-US festival screening voids eligibility. Free, with cash prizes and Cannes support on the winner's first feature. Submission note: own portal: 'My Account' at festival-cannes.com. Confirmed - film-school-only submission section of Cannes; no FilmFreeway. 2027 deadline Feb 15, 2027.

festivals.name: Cannes — Short Films in Competition 2027
festivals.why: At 13 minutes the film clears the hard 15-minute cap. Home-country screenings are allowed — Sundance does NOT void it; internet release or any non-US festival screening does (a Clermont screening would — see the France lock). The 12-month rule wants a mid-2026 completion date: enter with final deliverables. Free. Submission note: own portal: 'My Account' at festival-cannes.com. Confirmed - same portal as all Cannes Official Selection sections; not FilmFreeway.

festivals.name: Durban IFF 48th
festivals.why: Africa's premier Oscar-qualifying door for live-action shorts (Best Short Film). Open to all countries. Age-rule is borderline for a Jan 2026 film — submit early and confirm with the festival.

festivals.name: Indy Shorts 2027
festivals.why: Largest Midwest shorts festival; $5,000 Narrative Grand Prize; premiere status explicitly irrelevant; humanity-forward programming matches the redemption arc.

festivals.name: BlackStar 2027
festivals.why: The single best-fit festival in the lane: visionary Black/Brown/Indigenous cinema, diaspora spirituality, formally bold craft. Student fee waived; premiere preferred, not required. Requires burned-in open captions on the final print — a deliverable to plan.

festivals.name: DGA Student Awards 2027
festivals.why: The 2027 window should cover films made Sept 2025–Dec 2026 — containing a Jan 2026 completion. Director must be from a marginalized community and within a year of graduation at a US school. Verify the window when rules post ~Nov 1. Submission note: own portal: dga.org's own online application (exact submission-form subdomain is only exposed during the open application window, roughly Nov-Apr). Confirmed no FilmFreeway page exists for DGA Student Film Awards after targeted search; contact students@dga.org for current cycle link.

festivals.name: Student Academy Awards 54th
festivals.why: Going for the 54th (2027) cycle: medal winners become Oscar-eligible without needing a festival win. Published windows key on completion-for-credit dates — the same school-film date argument applies. Verify the 54th rules the day they post (~spring 2027) and confirm what AFI certifies.

festivals.name: BronzeLens 18th
festivals.why: Atlanta's premier Black film festival, qualifying via Best Short; realistic odds and low fees. Sequence with Atlanta FF (April) — ATLFF first, BronzeLens accepts non-premieres.

festivals.name: Curtas Vila do Conde 35th
festivals.why: Premier European competitive shorts festival, free to enter, qualifying via its Grand Prix, and only a Portuguese premiere required — slots cleanly after any US premiere.

festivals.name: TIFF Short Cuts 2027
festivals.why: By TIFF's own definitions, US-only screenings leave a US film at 'International Premiere' — Sundance-first stays compatible. The completion cutoff (~Sep 2026 by pattern) is the hardest date argument on the board: enter with the final-deliverables date and let programming decide. Keep it off the internet viewable in North America.

festivals.name: Venice — Orizzonti Corti 2027
festivals.why: On the board at Luke's call, constraint stated plainly: Orizzonti takes world premieres only — no public screening anywhere, ever — and no completion-date argument changes that rule. Viable only in the branch where the film is still unscreened by May 2027. Submission note: own portal: La Biennale's own registration system (web9.labiennale.org/selezione[year]/). Confirmed via official Biennale Cinema 'Submitting a film' pages for recent editions; not FilmFreeway. 2027 edition-specific subpage not yet published as of Sept 2026.

festivals.name: Aesthetica 17th
festivals.why: One of the few qualifying festivals where craft is a headline award — a named Best Cinematography prize — plus BAFTA and BIFA qualification and no premiere demands.

festivals.name: New Orleans FF 2027
festivals.why: Best regional-culture fit on the circuit: Deep South audience, Black Southern storytelling focus, qualifying jury award, no premiere requirement — and NOFF pays screening fees for selected shorts.

festivals.name: HollyShorts 23rd
festivals.why: Qualifies in four categories with a dedicated cinematography strand — but now requires an LA premiere, so it is mutually exclusive with ABFF and PAFF. Only one LA door gets the film; the Playbook recommends ABFF.

festivals.name: AMAA 2027
festivals.why: Africa's biggest film-award body; films that already screened or won elsewhere are explicitly eligible, so it costs nothing strategically. The strongest Nigerian-industry prestige credential available to a short.

festivals.name: AFI FEST 2027 + Conservatory Showcase
festivals.why: KOM is NOT in the announced 2026 Showcase lineup (verified against all 23 titles), so the home-turf path is the 2027 cycle — internal AFI selection, plus the open call. A Showcase screening is a public exhibition: sequence it after the premiere plays out.

festivals.name: Chicago Intl 63rd
festivals.why: Gold Hugo qualifies, and the long-running Black Perspectives program makes this a natural submission. No premiere required.

festivals.name: ADIFF NY 2027
festivals.why: A 30-year Harlem institution whose audience reads Yoruba cosmology fluently; free entry, four-city reach. Requires at least a NY premiere — sequence against Urbanworld.

festivals.name: Winterthur 31st
festivals.why: Switzerland's largest shorts festival, triple-qualifying with CHF 57,000 in prizes, nearly free to enter. Swiss premiere required — easy to preserve.

festivals.name: Urbanworld 2027
festivals.why: NYC's flagship multicultural festival with studio/streamer presence; Best Narrative Short (U.S.) qualifies. Requires World/USA/East-Coast/NY premiere status — this is the door the NY premiere should be saved for.

festivals.name: AFRIFF 2027
festivals.why: The director's home industry: Yoruba subject matter by a Nigerian director is core AFRIFF programming, with Nollywood market visibility. The 2026 edition was deliberately passed to protect the premiere; 2027 is the play.

festivals.name: Palm Springs ShortFest 2027
festivals.why: The biggest shorts-only festival/market in North America and the standard AFI-thesis launchpad. Five qualifying awards including Best Live-Action Short ≤15 Minutes — the film's exact bucket. No premiere requirement; already-online films eligible.

festivals.name: S16 Film Festival 2027
festivals.why: Run by the Surreal16 collective (C.J. Obasi, Abba Makama, Michael Omonua) — the exact lineage of chiaroscuro Yoruba-spiritual cinema. The 2026 window closed before the campaign started; 2027 is the play. Nigerian premiere required — sequence after AFRIFF decisions, not before. Submission note: No independent official festival domain could be verified (checked directly, plus linktr.ee/s16film which lists no separate website). Festival's only confirmed web presence beyond social media (@s16filmfestival on IG/X) is its FilmFreeway page; organized by the Surreal16 Collective (Lagos, Nigeria). Recommend treating the FilmFreeway page as the de facto official portal until/unless a dedicated domain surfaces.

festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Shorts Jury Award, Live Action
festivals.why: Qualifying in all three shorts categories with no premiere requirement and a student category. 2026 closed Jul 15; the Oct 2027 edition lands after the 100th window — next-cycle value.

festivals.name: SCAD Savannah Film Festival
festivals.benchNote: Awards-season showcase with real craft prizes for shorts — a named Best Cinematography award ($1,000, sponsored by ShotDeck) and a Jury Award for Excellence in Cinematography — plus a Southern setting…

festivals.name: International Short Film Festival Oberhausen
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Grand Prize of the City of Oberhausen
festivals.cat: Oldest shorts fest on earth · Oscar-qualifying
festivals.why: The world's oldest short film festival, free to enter, qualifying, German-premiere rule untouched by US screenings. Curation is avant-garde-first — frame the ritual and spiritual formal elements. Entering forecloses other German festivals first (collides with Hamburg). Submission note: Uses FilmChief portal, not FilmFreeway; deadline confirmed, open date unpublished.

festivals.name: Charleston Film Festival
festivals.benchNote: Honest verdict: noise. Despite Charleston being the most historically resonant city imaginable for this story (the largest slave port in North America), this festival is a small two-day event (Sept 25…

festivals.name: NBCUniversal Short Film Festival (2027)
festivals.outVerdict: Dormant — no confirmed editions; re-check only if news breaks.

festivals.name: Indie Memphis Film Festival
festivals.outVerdict: Great Southern room, no live-action qualifying path — winnable-circuit next ring, not this list.

festivals.name: International Film Festival Rotterdam — Ammodo Tiger Short Competition
festivals.why: A genuine A-list slot — the Tiger Short Competition is among Europe's most prestigious. Requires at minimum a European premiere (a US-only history preserves it) and its dates collide with Sundance. A deliberate Europe-first pivot, not a default: deadline Sep 15. Submission note: Direct IFFR portal, not FilmFreeway; late-fee deadline confirmed.

festivals.name: RiverRun International Film Festival
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying for animated + documentary shorts ONLY — no live-action path
festivals.why: Respected Winston-Salem festival 200 miles from where the story is set. The Academy list settles it: no live-action narrative award qualifies, so this is regional resonance and press, not an Oscar play. NC premiere required — intact.

festivals.name: Sidewalk Film Festival
festivals.why: Birmingham's flagship since 1999 with a dedicated Black Lens program for Black filmmakers and $10k+ in cash awards. No Oscar path — reinstated on Joan's case: Deep South audience resonance and a winnable student category.

festivals.name: Morehouse College Human Rights Film Festival (MCHRFF)
festivals.outVerdict: Thematic bullseye but Oscar-qualifying status has lapsed (not on the 99th list) — community submission at best.

festivals.name: Smithsonian NMAAHC — Smithsonian African American Film Festival (SAAFF)
festivals.outVerdict: Dormant since the 2018 inaugural edition; unreachable.

festivals.name: BAFTA Student Awards (2027)
festivals.loc: Los Angeles (BAFTA North America), USA / UK
festivals.outVerdict: Likely defunct since 2023 after BAFTA restructured its North America programs.

festivals.name: BFI London Film Festival — Short Film Competition (71st edition)
festivals.outVerdict: UK and Irish films only — a US-produced AFI thesis cannot submit.

festivals.name: New Voices in Black Cinema (BAM / ActNow Foundation)
festivals.outVerdict: Dormant — BAM festival page 404s; no confirmed edition.

festivals.name: Middleburg Film Festival
festivals.outVerdict: Curated awards-season features event; no open shorts lane.

festivals.name: Princess Grace Awards — Film (thesis honoraria)
festivals.outVerdict: School-nominated scholarships for upcoming thesis work; nomination window passed.

festivals.name: SFFILM 2027
festivals.cat: Longest-running fest in the Americas · Oscar-qualifying
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Golden Gate Award for Best Narrative Short
festivals.why: Founded 1957; blue-chip curatorial brand whose premiere bar is only Bay Area — prior screenings elsewhere cost nothing. Highly selective: a reach, not a banker.

festivals.name: San Francisco Black FF 2027
festivals.why: Founded 1998 by publicist Ave Montague with a $200 budget; a beloved Juneteenth-tied community festival, now family-run. Diaspora audience-building at low cost.

festivals.name: LA Shorts Fest 2027
festivals.cat: LA institution · qualifies via Best of Fest only
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying awards: Best of Fest / Animation / Documentary / International — a US fiction short's only route is Best of Fest
festivals.why: Longest-running shorts festival in LA (1997), 69 alumni Oscar nominations. The 2027 edition MOVED to March 4–10 (it ran in July previously) — so it now sits weeks after PAFF and Slamdance in the LA calendar, tightening the one-LA-premiere problem rather than easing it. Requires no prior LA County screening. Submissions are open now, final deadline Jan 22, 2027.

festivals.name: San Jose Int'l Short FF 2027
festivals.cat: Boutique shorts fest · qualifies after this window
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best of the Fest only; Oct 2027 dates land after the 100th-Awards window
festivals.why: MovieMaker 'worth the entry fee' pick. A win here counts toward the 101st Oscars, not the 100th — second-year backstop.

festivals.name: San Luis Obispo IFF 2027
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying for Best Documentary Short ONLY — no narrative path
festivals.why: Respected regional with $500 cash prizes in the George Sidney competition and no premiere requirement. Worth $30 as exposure and a possible cash prize; not an Oscar play for a fiction short.

festivals.name: Santa Fe IFF 2027
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best Narrative Short (+$15,000 Panavision package + $500 cash); Oct 2027 lands after the 100th window
festivals.why: Newly qualifying since Oct 2024 in New Mexico's production hub, with softer competition than coastal qualifiers. The 2026 edition closed Jul 9 — this records the 2027 edition, which feeds the following cycle.

festivals.name: Ann Arbor FF 65th
festivals.cat: Oldest avant-garde fest · narrative qualifying path
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Lawrence Kasdan Award for Best Narrative Film (+ Ken Burns Best of Fest)
festivals.why: Founded 1963, ~$40,000 in awards, no premiere requirement. Curation is experimental-first — frame the film around its ritual and spiritual formal elements. Late deadline Sep 30, 2026 is still open.

festivals.name: MSPIFF 45
festivals.why: Running since 1981, 200+ films for a big Twin Cities audience. With the student discount and a known fee-waiver email, likely the best cost-per-audience ratio on Joan's sheet. Note: FilmFreeway lists this as the 46th edition, not the 45th — same Apr 2027 dates.

festivals.name: Montclair FF 2027
festivals.why: Founded 2012 with the Colbert family as backers; trade press calls it an early Oscar proving ground for features. High-credibility NYC-adjacent exposure rare at this price. Joan ranked it #1 in New Jersey.

festivals.name: Teaneck IFF 2027
festivals.why: Founded 2006, themed 'Activism: Making Change'; programs heavily around racial-justice history. A story of enslavement, faith and resistance is a near-perfect mission fit — position it as social-justice storytelling in the cover note.

festivals.name: Ashland Independent FF 26th
festivals.path: No qualifying path (did not survive its financial crisis)
festivals.why: Historically a filmmaker-hospitality standout; a reorganized board eliminated the debt and is rebuilding at roughly half the former footprint. Southern-Oregon-only premiere bar. Price the laurel at post-crisis value.

festivals.name: Dirty Popcorn Black FF 2027
festivals.why: Two-day showcase hosted by the Delaware Art Museum. Free to submit; stated priority is BIPOC filmmakers from DE/MD/NJ/PA/NY. Verify a 2026 edition actually ran before counting on 2027.

festivals.name: Gary Int'l Black FF 16th
festivals.why: Founded ~2010, 30 minutes from Chicago, backed by the mayor's office, with genuine Chicagoland Black audience reach. CORRECTION: the extended ENTRY deadline was Aug 23, 2026 and has passed — the Sep 21 date is materials-in-hand for films already accepted. Target the 2027 edition, or email the festival.

festivals.name: Twin Cities Black FF 2027
festivals.cat: Longest-standing Black fest in the Upper Midwest
festivals.why: Founded ~2002 by Natalie Morrow; small (~1,000 attendees, 3 awards) but 24 years running. The official site is stale while FilmFreeway is active — one email before paying.

festivals.name: Newark Black FF 2027
festivals.cat: Oldest Black film festival in the US (1974)
festivals.path: No qualifying path; juried Paul Robeson Awards (historically biennial — confirm cycle)
festivals.why: Run by The Newark Museum of Art annually since 1974; early platforms for Spike Lee, Barry Jenkins, Ava DuVernay. 'Official selection of America's oldest Black film festival' is a laurel with historical weight, and the museum setting suits a period drama about ancestral faith.

festivals.name: North Carolina Black FF 25th
festivals.why: Presented by Wilmington's Black Arts Alliance for 24 consecutive years, drawing entries from NC to Kenya. A South Carolina story plays close to home in a legacy production town.

festivals.name: Greater Cleveland Urban FF 16th
festivals.why: Founded 2012; nine days in-person plus virtual means real audience exposure, not one slot. Submission window runs Feb 1–May 31 every year — calendar February.

festivals.name: Greenwood FF 2027
festivals.why: Launched June 2021 — the Tulsa Race Massacre centennial — in the historic Greenwood district, with OSU-Tulsa as sponsor. A film about an enslaved man reclaiming ancestral faith, screening where Black self-determination was burned and rebuilt: unmatched narrative alignment.

festivals.name: Tallgrass FF 2027 — Gordon Parks Award
festivals.cat: Named award for Black excellence · free entry
festivals.path: Gordon Parks Award for Black Excellence in Filmmaking — Short Film (category added 2025; short-film prize amount unconfirmed)
festivals.why: The award honors the pioneering Black photographer-director whose period craft mirrors this film's, backed by the Kansas African American Museum and the Wichita NAACP. Feature-level winners get $5,000 + $15,000 Panavision rental.

festivals.name: Seattle Black FF 2027
festivals.why: Founded 2003 as the Langston Hughes African American Film Festival; renamed 2020 explicitly to embrace the whole Black diaspora — a Nigerian-directed Yoruba story is what the rebrand courts. Run by LANGSTON at the city-owned institute.

festivals.name: Denton Black FF 13th
festivals.why: Founded 2015, now a major regional draw — film, music, spoken word, tech expo. The college category means competing against student work in a big Southern Black market during Black History Month season.

festivals.name: Roxbury Int'l FF 2027
festivals.cat: New England's largest fest for filmmakers of color
festivals.why: Running since ~1998; screens inside the Museum of Fine Arts Boston as an official partner — museum-grade curatorial validation for a high-craft period drama, in Boston's academic and Black arts community.

festivals.name: Cascade Festival of African Films 37th
festivals.cat: Longest-running African film fest in the US
festivals.why: Founded 1991 by Portland Community College faculty; 36 consecutive editions, always free to the public. A month-long run means genuine community audience for $5. Confirmed OPEN for the 37th edition — deadline Sep 21, 2026 has not passed.

festivals.name: British Urban FF 2027
festivals.why: Founded 2005; 20th-anniversary Screen Daily profile. The UK beachhead — London's large Nigerian diaspora, with trade-press attention rare at this size. Mid-transition (new leadership, date move): some execution risk.

festivals.name: Africa Film Fest Australia 2027
festivals.why: Founded ~2023 by Kenyan-Australian filmmakers with Screen NSW backing; 2026 ran at the Sydney Opera House. The shorts category is explicitly for filmmakers of African heritage — the director qualifies directly. $12.49 buys a third continent.

festivals.name: Int'l African FF in Argentina 15th
festivals.why: Run by nonprofit Observatorio Sur (~14 editions) across three cities plus a tour. Essentially the only Latin American window for African-diaspora cinema; the Yoruba thread resonates with Afro-Latin religious traditions. Spanish subtitles likely required.

festivals.name: Kurzfilm Festival Hamburg 43rd
festivals.why: Scrappy, respected, more narrative-friendly than Oberhausen. German-premiere rule for the international competition collides with Oberhausen — Germany goes to one of them. Tightest completion window of the group: production not older than Jan 2026.

festivals.name: Warsaw FF 2027
festivals.cat: A-list features fest · qualifying shorts sidebar
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Grand Prix + Best Live Action Short; Oct 2027 lands after the 100th window
festivals.why: FIAPF A-list with four qualifying shorts awards. The 2026 edition closed Jul 31 and Oct 2027 feeds the following cycle — recorded for the long campaign.

festivals.name: In the Palace 24th
festivals.cat: Bulgaria's flagship shorts fest · Oscar + SAA qualifying
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best Short Fiction (main competition; the student track feeds the Student Academy Awards instead)
festivals.why: Qualifying since 2017 and cheap. Category trap: enter the MAIN fiction competition (or both) — the student category alone doesn't reach the Oscar award. Bulgarian premiere intact. Deadline Oct 1.

festivals.name: Drama ISFF 2027
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Grand Prix, International Competition; BAFTA (new 2026) + EFA qualifying
festivals.why: Greece's leading shorts festival for nearly 50 years — early platform for Lanthimos and Villeneuve. Greek premiere preserved by a US-only history. Its Sep 2027 dates land days before the window closes: a win counts, with zero slack.

festivals.name: Anonimul IFF 2027
festivals.cat: Danube Delta indie · hosts one guest
festivals.path: No qualifying path; no premiere requirement
festivals.why: Romania's 'Danube Delta Sundance' (est. 2004), ~5,000 attendees. Free entry, and the festival covers accommodation for one team member if selected. A free bonus, not a pillar. Submission note: No FilmFreeway; submit by email to festival@anonimul.ro with entry form.

festivals.name: BAFICI 2027
festivals.cat: Latin America's premier indie festival · free entry
festivals.why: 400+ titles for a huge cinephile audience since 1999. Free entry to genuine critical credibility without spending any premiere that matters. A long international run by April could soften selection odds. Submission note: Own portal at bafici.org, not FilmFreeway; 28th unannounced, shifted.

festivals.name: Vancouver IFF 2027
festivals.path: Not on the Academy qualifying list (verified against every Canadian entry)
festivals.why: One of North America's largest audience festivals. Joan's sheet marked it qualifying — it isn't, and both reachable editions miss the 100th window anyway. Recorded as exposure for the long campaign.

festivals.name: Montréal FNC 2027
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best Short Film, International Competition (Loup Argenté); Oct 2027 feeds the following cycle
festivals.why: Founded 1971; a prestigious auteur/avant-garde house whose taste for formally bold, culturally hybrid work could embrace the film's Yoruba spiritual dimension. Quebec premiere intact.

festivals.name: Show Me Shorts 2027
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best International Film; Oct 2027 feeds the following cycle
festivals.why: New Zealand's leading shorts festival and its first Academy-accredited one — a warm nationwide tour. International films explicitly eligible for the qualifying award. A low-cost hedge for a campaign that extends.

festivals.name: Busan Int'l Short FF 44th
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Grand Prix in International Competition (KRW 10,000,000; winner-take-all)
festivals.why: Korea's premier shorts festival at the Busan Cinema Center, also BAFTA/Goya-qualifying. Korean premiere required for international competition — intact. A cheap, genuine qualifying lottery ticket.

festivals.name: Short Shorts FF & Asia 2027
festivals.cat: One of Asia's largest · five qualifying awards
festivals.path: Oscar-qualifying — Best Short awards in International / Asia International / Japan / Animation / Non-Fiction
festivals.why: Founded 1999 by Tetsuya Bessho; George Lucas Award Grand Prix. Multiple qualifying categories beat single-award fests on odds. Japan premiere must hold until ~June 2027: no Japan screenings, no streaming with Japanese subtitles. US screenings fine.

festivals.name: ISC Award Osaka 2027
festivals.cat: Student award · flights + hotel for finalists
festivals.path: No qualifying path; student-enrollment eligibility — confirm post-graduation rules
festivals.why: Run by Osaka's Knowledge Capital: ~1,000 entries from 88 countries, six winners, and finalists get roundtrip flights plus accommodation. The 2026 window closed Jul 31 — this records 2027; confirm films made while enrolled still qualify.
